title: Grateful Dead Live at Pauley Pavilion - University of California on 1973-11-17

ai_review.summary: Virtually perfect Ashley soundboard captures a stellar November ’73 show highlighted by an epic Here Comes Sunshine and a soaring Ramble on Rose.
ai_review.review: The recording, restored by Jay Ashley, delivers crystal‑clear soundboard fidelity that lets the band’s late‑1973 fire shine through. The performance is consistently strong – Jerry’s surf‑tone guitar on HCS, Keith’s sparkling piano on Ramble on Rose and a tight rhythm section make the second set transitions feel effortless, even if a few first‑set moments are noted as uneven or flubbed.

ai_rating.rationale: The bulk of detailed reviews (8 out of 10) award 4–5 stars, praising both the musical performance and the Ashley soundboard restoration; only one reviewer notes harsh recording quality, so overall rating is very high.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Jay Ashley’s restoration is described as virtually perfect, crisp and balanced. One reviewer mentions a “harsh, jarring” quality reminiscent of DP‑33, but the consensus is that the tape sounds clean, warm and highly listenable.

standout_songs: Morning Dew (noted for its intensity despite flubs)
poor_songs: Morning Dew (flubs and tuning issues mentioned)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds a relaxed yet urgent groove with strong HCS and tight ensemble playing; second set is praised for seamless transitions, especially Row Jimmy → Jack Straw → Ramble on Rose, delivering a high‑energy climax.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as pure surf‑guitar mode on HCS, ‘mission to Mars’ tone, occasional lyrical flubs but overall inspiring lead work.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is called “amazing”, provides solid bombs on Ramble on Rose and drives the groove throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s vocals get an “edgy” nod on Around; his solo on Jack Straw is praised though some reviewers note later vocal fatigue.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's piano shines – great tinkling on Ramble on Rose, strong accompaniment on HCS and overall jazzy mastery noted.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann (and Mickey Hart where applicable) receive praise for solid, “good” playing, especially on Jack Straw.
